## What this is

- **A scheduled fixture-replay canary per parser family (BL-025 canary part; SIG-PARSE-007/008, RISK-P7-06).** `tests/parser_canary/spec.toml` (`sig.parser-canary-spec/1`) declares ten families — every connectors module shipping a `canary_findings` deterministic core (`osm`, `atlas`, `accountability`, `audit_structural` ×4 file-kinds, `dot_511`, `flock_portal`) plus a `parsing.drift` structural family — over a sealed corpus of real captured samples. `sig-ops parser-canary` (`check`/`run`/`scheduled`/`job`) replays each family's own parse + canary path; the module allow-list refuses arbitrary imports.
- **A typed issue on drift.** Every non-clean family lands a `sig.parser-canary-issue/1` entry (`parser_drift` on findings, `canary_error` on a failed replay — a closed vocabulary deliberately parallel to J3 §7.3's; a parser family is not an ingest source) inside `sig.parser-canary-report/1`, plus the shared `sig.probe-run/1` envelope and the recorded-alert seam (`parser-canary` kind, ADR-077). A mutated fixture raises `parser_drift` — the checked acceptance shape.
- **The permanent job + trigger, declared.** `ops/parser_canary.toml` (`sig.parser-canary/1`): `sig-parser-canary` on `sig-quality-probe-rt` (conditioned `ops/probes/` objectCreator only; no DB, no capture read; `sig-alert-webhook-token` the one secret), `sig-sched-parser-canary` daily 01:45Z days 1–5/14–31 — structurally outside both OM-19 windows; the job re-checks them in-container. `ops/gcp/parser-canary.sh` owns the windowed mutations (deploy → trigger → the canary run itself → verify; name-checked rollback). The corpus rides the image (`tests/parser_canary/` COPYed into `/app`).
- **The named mutation stays QUEUED `prepared_not_executed`.** GATE-G6 §4 (2026-11-05T15:20Z, "Approve all 15") names P37.15 — pre-authorised in-ticket under the contract's own preconditions, restore point and rollback — but `SIG_GCP_PROJECT`/ADC are absent, so `--apply` exits before any mutation.
